Why hasn't there been a major financial crisis in recent years? | Idea Farm

Deutsche Bank

Henry Allen, Peter Sidorov

## 18 Pages

- November 2026 

Deutsche Bank examines why there has been no major financial crisis since 2008, despite Minsky’s warning that long stretches of stability breed risk taking. The authors credit post crisis bank reforms, a shift of assets toward nonbanks and faster policy intervention, then weigh AI leverage, private credit and stretched sovereign balance sheets as candidates for the next crisis.

## Key Takeaways

Banks Hold Less: Banks' share of financial assets fell from 46% in 2008 to 38% in 2024, while nonbanks rose from 43% to 51%.

Debt Moved To Governments: Since 2007, government debt went from the smallest to the largest of four global debt categories, narrowing room for future intervention.

AI Leverage Watch: DB projections put US business leverage near the GHSS red zone by 2028, a zone linked to a 45% crisis risk within three years.
